scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9022: Hi IT!! My connection from pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) to pc_0_1
(10.0.1.2) keeps DROPPING AND RECONNECTING, over and over -- the infra people
say "the sessions across the fabric keep bouncing" and I believe them,
because that is EXACTLY what it feels like!! Those switch-to-switch
connections are obviously coming up and down nonstop between the racks --
nothing stays connected for five minutes!! Please go through the fabric,
clear the bouncing neighbors, and make the sessions STAY UP -- I cannot work
in bursts!!!

  occurring -- does the agent check the BGP session uptimes against the live

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- BGP sessions flapping across the fabric -- is
NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss across
the fabric. The leaf<->spine and spine<->super_spine BGP sessions are Established
with steady uptime (no recent resets), the prefix counts are stable, and there are
no flap/withdraw churn signs in the routing tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the BGP sessions are stable, the path
is healthy, and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (sustained ping pc_0_1 from pc_0_0,
inspect the BGP neighbor uptimes/states on the leaf and spine routers), finds them
stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- declaring
adjacencies flapping or clearing neighbors to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — BGP sessions across the DC CLOS fabric repeatedly dropping and reconnecting — is not confirmed by any live or historical evidence. A complete sweep across all diagnostic layers found the following: (1) End-to-end reachability between pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) shows 0 % packet loss in both directions. (2) All five FRR routers (leaf_router_0_0, leaf_router_0_1, spine_router_0_0, spine_router_0_1, super_spine_router_0) are healthy — watchfrr, zebra, and bgpd are all running on every device. (3) All ten BGP eBGP sessions across the fabric are in the Established state and have held steady since lab startup (~3 minutes); detailed neighbor output confirms "Connections established 1; dropped 0" and zero BGP Notifications sent or received on every sampled session. (4) BGP hold timers are 180 s (keepalive 60 s) — standard values that are not susceptible to spurious expiry. (5) No flap-inducing processes or stress tools are running on any device. (6) L2 identity is clean (no duplicate MACs, no down interfaces), and no traffic-control shaping or ACL drops are present anywhere in the fabric. Per the intermittent-fault ruling criteria, a claim of repeated session bouncing requires at minimum a flap mechanism (process, misconfigured timer, link fault) or historical traces (non-zero drop counters, BGP Notifications, elevated carrier changes). None of these indicators exist. The BGP fabric is operating correctly; the user's report is unconfirmed.

Root cause: No anomaly is present — the BGP fabric has been stable since startup with zero session drops and no fault mechanism capable of causing the described behavior.

Fix: No corrective action is required. If the user experiences genuine reconnection events in the future, collect BGP log output (`log file /var/log/frr/bgpd.log` in FRR configuration) and carrier-change counters at the time of the event to identify a real trigger.
